claim_text: Lloyds Bank's app and online banking stopped working for many customers on Nov 27
summary: On the morning of Friday Nov 27, many Lloyds Bank customers could not log in to the app or online banking, make payments or check balances. At 12:50 GMT the bank was still working to fix it and had not said it was fixed.
detail: Lloyds has not said how many customers were affected or which parts of its systems failed.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The Independent: customers "were unable to make payments, check their balance" or use the app; at 12:50 GMT it says Lloyds "confirmed it was working to resolve the technical problems"; The Register (12:01 GMT) reports the same.

claim_text: Lloyds Banking Group says some customers are having difficulty accessing the app
summary: A Lloyds Banking Group spokesperson said: "We're aware some customers are having difficulty accessing the app this morning. We're sorry for the inconvenience and are working to get things back to normal as quickly as possible."
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The Register and London Loves Tech quote the same spokesperson statement word for word.

claim_text: Bank of Scotland's app and online banking had problems too
summary: Bank of Scotland, another bank in Lloyds Banking Group, also had problems with its app and online banking. It said on its service status page: "We're aware some customers are having issues with our app and online banking at the moment."
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The Register quotes Bank of Scotland's status page; The Independent says Bank of Scotland "also appeared to be hit by the problems"; London Loves Tech says Bank of Scotland "was also affected".

claim_text: Nobody has given a cause or said it was a cyberattack
summary: Neither Lloyds Banking Group nor any outlet has given a cause. Error messages in the app spoke of "technical problems", and no one has said the outage was an attack.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The Register reports the bank's statement with no cause; The Independent says one error message "blamed 'technical problems'"; London Loves Tech says some customers saw an error about an "ongoing technical problem". None mentions an attack.

claim_text: Outage reports began around 9:40 to 10 AM GMT, with more than 4,000 for Lloyds
summary: Reports of problems on the outage tracker Downdetector began around 9:40 to 10 AM GMT on Nov 27. London Loves Tech counted more than 4,000 reports for Lloyds and more than 300 for Bank of Scotland by 10:16 AM.
detail: Downdetector counts reports from users, not the number of people affected.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: London Loves Tech: "More than 4,000 reports of problems with Lloyds" and "The first complaints emerged at around 9.40am"; The Independent: "Problems started around 10am in the UK, according to tracking website Down Detector".

claim_text: The bank suggested clearing the browser cache or reinstalling the app
summary: The bank told customers to clear their browser cache and history and reinstall the app if problems continued. Some customers could sign in through the website or another browser, but not all.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: London Loves Tech: "The bank suggested clearing browser cache and history, and reinstalling the app if the problem persisted" and "switching browsers had allowed them to log in".

claim_text: Lloyds Banking Group has more than 21 million app users
summary: Lloyds Banking Group said late last year it had more than 21 million mobile app users and over 23 million digitally active customers, The Register reports. The Independent says Lloyds has around 28 million customers across its brands.
detail: The two figures count different things.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The Register: "more than 21 million mobile app users and over 23 million digitally active customers"; The Independent: "Lloyds says it has around 28 million customers, across its different brands".

claim_text: A Lloyds app fault exposed some transactions to other users earlier in 2026
summary: Earlier in 2026 a faulty software update at Lloyds Banking Group may have shown almost 448,000 app users other customers' transactions. The group blamed a software defect. No source links it to this outage.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The Register: a botched software update "potentially exposed other customers' transaction information to almost 448,000 app users" and the bank "blamed a defect in the API handling transaction data".

claim_text: Lloyds Bank is a large British retail bank in Lloyds Banking Group
summary: Lloyds Bank is a large British retail and commercial bank, founded in Birmingham in 1765, and a key part of Lloyds Banking Group.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Wikipedia: Lloyds Bank "is a major British retail and commercial bank", established in Birmingham in 1765, and "a key subsidiary of Lloyds Banking Group".

claim_text: The app told customers Lloyds was working to get everything back to normal
summary: City AM says customers trying to log in to the Lloyds app saw a message: "We know that some of our customers are having issues logging into online banking and our app", with an apology and a promise to fix it soon.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: City AM (updated 12:43 GMT): "a message read: 'We know that some of our customers are having issues logging into online banking and our app. We are sorry about this...'".

claim_text: No source links the Lloyds outage to the DWP cyber incident the same morning
summary: City AM notes that the outage came on the same morning as a cyber incident at the Department for Work and Pensions that took some government online services offline. It does not say the two are connected, and nobody else has.
detail: Lloyds has given no cause for its outage; City AM says it contacted Lloyds for comment.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: City AM: "It also coincided with a 'cyber incident' at the Department of Work and Pensions"; it reports no link and says "Lloyds has been contacted for comment".
